ko.title: [Consumer Psychology #7] 무엇을 말하는가만큼 누가 말하는가가 중요한 이유: 광고에서의 출처 효과

segments.src: > The same message can persuade more or less depending on who delivers it. We judge a source by expertise, trustworthiness, attractiveness, and whether they "fit" the product.
segments.tr: > 같은 메시지라도 누가 전달하느냐에 따라 설득력이 달라질 수 있다. 우리는 출처를 전문성, 신뢰성, 매력도, 그리고 제품과 "어울리는지" 여부로 판단한다.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 오늘의 개념

segments.src: Imagine two people telling you a new sunscreen is great.
segments.tr: 새로운 선크림이 정말 좋다고 말하는 두 사람을 상상해 보자.

segments.src: One is a dermatologist.
segments.tr: 한 명은 피부과 전문의다.

segments.src: The other is a stranger in a parking lot.
segments.tr: 다른 한 명은 주차장에서 마주친 낯선 사람이다.

segments.src: The words are identical, but you probably trust one more.
segments.tr: 두 사람의 말은 똑같지만, 아마 당신은 전문의의 말을 더 신뢰할 것이다.

segments.src: Psychologists call this the **source effect**: who delivers a message changes how persuasive it is.
segments.tr: 심리학에서는 이를 **출처 효과**라고 부른다. 메시지를 누가 전달하느냐에 따라 그 메시지의 설득력이 달라진다는 뜻이다.

segments.src: Research going back to Carl Hovland and his colleagues at Yale in the 1950s points to a few main qualities people look for in a source.
segments.tr: 1950년대 예일대학교의 칼 호블랜드(Carl Hovland)와 동료들의 연구에서 시작된 연구들은, 사람들이 출처에서 찾는 몇 가지 주요 자질을 짚어 준다.

segments.src: Credibility.** Credibility has two parts:
segments.tr: 신뢰도(Credibility).** 신뢰도는 두 가지 요소로 이루어진다:

segments.src: - **Expertise** asks whether this person knows what they are talking about. A mechanic recommending motor oil carries weight.
segments.tr: - **전문성(Expertise)**은 이 사람이 실제로 잘 아는지를 묻는다. 엔진오일을 추천하는 정비사는 무게가 있다.

segments.src: - **Trustworthiness** asks whether this person is being honest with you. People trust a source more when it seems to have nothing to gain. That's why "I'm not paid to say this" is such a common line, and why a reviewer who points out a product's flaws can come across as *more* believable.
segments.tr: - **신뢰성(Trustworthiness)**은 이 사람이 나에게 솔직한지를 묻는다. 사람들은 출처가 얻을 것이 없어 보일 때 더 신뢰한다. 그래서 "이 말로 돈을 받은 게 아닙니다"라는 말이 흔하게 쓰이고, 제품의 단점을 짚는 리뷰어가 *더* 믿을 만하게 느껴지기도 한다.

segments.src: Attractiveness.** This covers more than looks.
segments.tr: 매력도(Attractiveness).** 이는 외모 이상을 의미한다.

segments.src: It includes being likable, being familiar, and seeming similar to you.
segments.tr: 호감이 가는지, 익숙한지, 나와 비슷해 보이는지도 포함된다.

segments.src: We tend to listen to people we like and people who seem "like us," and sometimes we copy them.
segments.tr: 우리는 호감 가는 사람이나 "나와 비슷한" 사람의 말에 귀 기울이는 경향이 있고, 때로는 그들을 따라 하기도 한다.

segments.src: That's part of why everyday-looking actors show up in so many ads.
segments.tr: 평범해 보이는 배우들이 수많은 광고에 등장하는 이유도 여기에 일부 있다.

segments.src: Fit (the match-up hypothesis).** A source works best when their image matches the product.
segments.tr: 적합성(Fit, 매칭 가설).** 출처의 이미지가 제품과 맞을 때 가장 효과적이다.

segments.src: A star athlete selling sports drinks feels natural.
segments.tr: 스포츠음료를 광고하는 유명 운동선수는 자연스럽게 느껴진다.

segments.src: The same athlete selling retirement annuities feels off.
segments.tr: 같은 선수가 노후 연금 상품을 광고하면 어색하게 느껴진다.

segments.src: Anthropologist Grant McCracken described a related idea called **meaning transfer**: a celebrity carries cultural meanings (toughness, luxury, humor), and an endorsement tries to move those meanings onto the brand.
segments.tr: 인류학자 그랜트 맥크래켄(Grant McCracken)은 관련 개념인 **의미 전이(meaning transfer)**를 제시했다. 유명인은 강인함, 고급스러움, 유머 같은 문화적 의미를 지니고 있고, 광고 모델 기용은 그 의미를 브랜드에 옮기려 한다.

segments.src: If the meanings don't match the product, the transfer falls flat.
segments.tr: 그 의미가 제품과 맞지 않으면 전이는 제대로 일어나지 않는다.

segments.src: **Celebrities vs.
segments.tr: **유명인 vs.

segments.src: influencers.** Celebrities bring instant attention and recognition.
segments.tr: 인플루언서.** 유명인은 즉각적인 주목과 인지도를 가져온다.

segments.src: They also carry risks: a scandal can drag the brand down with them, and a star who endorses many products can seem less sincere.
segments.tr: 하지만 위험도 따른다. 스캔들이 터지면 브랜드까지 함께 추락할 수 있고, 여러 제품을 홍보하는 스타는 진정성이 없어 보일 수 있다.

segments.src: Influencers often have smaller audiences, but their followers may feel a **parasocial relationship**, a one-sided sense of knowing them personally.
segments.tr: 인플루언서는 대체로 팔로워 수가 적지만, 팔로워들은 **파라소셜 관계(parasocial relationship)**, 즉 상대를 개인적으로 안다고 느끼는 일방적인 친밀감을 느낄 수 있다.

segments.src: That feeling of closeness can make a recommendation feel like advice from a friend.
segments.tr: 이런 친밀감 때문에 추천이 친구의 조언처럼 느껴질 수 있다.

segments.src: One more twist is the **sleeper effect**.
segments.tr: 여기에 한 가지 변수가 더 있는데, 바로 **수면자 효과(sleeper effect)**다.

segments.src: Sometimes a message from a low-credibility source gains persuasive power over time, because people remember the message but forget where it came from.
segments.tr: 신뢰도가 낮은 출처의 메시지가 시간이 지나면서 오히려 설득력을 얻는 경우가 있다. 사람들이 메시지는 기억하지만 출처는 잊어버리기 때문이다.

segments.src: Researchers have found the effect is real but shows up only under fairly specific conditions, so don't count on it as a strategy.
segments.tr: 연구자들은 이 효과가 실제로 존재하지만 꽤 특정한 조건에서만 나타난다는 것을 확인했으므로, 이를 전략으로 기대해서는 안 된다.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 일상 속에서

segments.src: Say you're scrolling TikTok and see a creator with about 80,000 followers raving about a $14 drugstore moisturizer.
segments.tr: 틱톡을 넘기다가 약 8만 명의 팔로워를 가진 크리에이터가 14달러짜리 드럭스토어 보습제를 극찬하는 영상을 봤다고 해 보자.

segments.src: She shows her bare skin, mentions she has dry patches like you, and says it beats the $60 department-store cream she used to buy.
segments.tr: 그녀는 맨얼굴을 보여 주며 당신처럼 건조한 부위가 있다고 말하고, 예전에 쓰던 60달러짜리 백화점 크림보다 낫다고 한다.

segments.src: Several source effects are at work here:
segments.tr: 여기에는 여러 출처 효과가 작용하고 있다:

segments.src: - **Similarity:** she has the same skin problem you do, so she feels "like you."
segments.tr: - **유사성:** 그녀는 당신과 같은 피부 고민이 있어서 "나와 비슷한" 사람처럼 느껴진다.

segments.src: - **Perceived honesty:** praising a cheaper product makes her seem less like she's selling something.
segments.tr: - **인지된 솔직함:** 더 저렴한 제품을 칭찬하면 무언가를 팔려는 사람처럼 보이지 않는다.

segments.src: - **Parasocial closeness:** you've watched her morning routine for months, so it feels like a tip from a friend.
segments.tr: - **파라소셜 친밀감:** 몇 달 동안 그녀의 아침 루틴을 지켜봐 왔기 때문에, 친구가 건네는 조언처럼 느껴진다.

segments.src: Now look for the small "#ad" or "Paid partnership" label.
segments.tr: 이제 작은 "#ad" 또는 "유료 파트너십" 표시를 찾아보자.

segments.src: The U.S.
segments.tr: 미국

segments.src: Federal Trade Commission (FTC) requires influencers to clearly disclose material connections to brands, such as payment or free products.
segments.tr: 연방거래위원회(FTC)는 인플루언서가 금전 지급이나 무료 제품 제공 등 브랜드와의 중요한 관계를 명확히 밝히도록 요구한다.

segments.src: Once you see that label, your sense of her trustworthiness may shift a bit.
segments.tr: 그 표시를 보고 나면 그 사람에 대한 신뢰감이 조금 달라질 수 있다.

segments.src: That's the source effect working in reverse.
segments.tr: 이것이 거꾸로 작동하는 출처 효과다.

segments.src: The product hasn't changed, but your read on the messenger has.
segments.tr: 제품은 바뀌지 않았지만, 메시지 전달자를 보는 당신의 시선은 바뀌었다.

segments.src: ## 3-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## 3줄 요약

segments.src: 1. Persuasion depends on the messenger as well as the message. People weigh a source's expertise, trustworthiness, and attractiveness.
segments.tr: 1. 설득은 메시지뿐 아니라 메시지 전달자에 따라서도 달라진다. 사람들은 출처의 전문성, 신뢰성, 매력도를 따져 본다.

segments.src: 2. Endorsers work best when their image fits the product (match-up hypothesis), because the celebrity's meaning carries over to the brand.
segments.tr: 2. 보증인(endorser)은 자신의 이미지가 제품과 맞을 때 가장 효과적이다(매칭 가설). 유명인의 의미가 브랜드로 전이되기 때문이다.

segments.src: 3. Influencers persuade through closeness and similarity. Disclosure rules like the FTC's exist so consumers know when that closeness is paid for.
segments.tr: 3. 인플루언서는 친밀감과 유사성을 통해 설득한다. FTC 같은 공개 규정은 그 친밀감에 돈이 오갔는지를 소비자가 알 수 있도록 하기 위해 존재한다.

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ 자기 점검 퀴즈

segments.src: **Q1.** A source's credibility is usually described as having two main components.
segments.tr: **Q1.** 출처의 신뢰도는 보통 두 가지 주요 요소로 설명된다.

segments.src: Which pair is correct?
segments.tr: 올바른 짝은 무엇인가?

segments.src: - A) Fame and wealth
segments.tr: - A) 명성과 재산

segments.src: - B) Expertise and trustworthiness
segments.tr: - B) 전문성과 신뢰성

segments.src: - C) Attractiveness and humor
segments.tr: - C) 매력도와 유머

segments.src: - D) Age and gender
segments.tr: - D) 나이와 성별

segments.src: (True/False)** According to the match-up hypothesis, the most famous celebrity available will always be the most effective endorser, whatever the product.
segments.tr: (참/거짓)** 매칭 가설에 따르면, 이용 가능한 가장 유명한 유명인이 제품과 무관하게 언제나 가장 효과적인 보증인이다.

segments.src: **Q3.** A follower feels like they personally "know" an influencer they've never met.
segments.tr: **Q3.** 팔로워는 한 번도 만난 적 없는 인플루언서를 개인적으로 "안다"고 느낀다.

segments.src: What is this called?
segments.tr: 이를 무엇이라고 하는가?

segments.src: - A) Sleeper effect
segments.tr: - A) 수면자 효과

segments.src: - B) Meaning transfer
segments.tr: - B) 의미 전이

segments.src: - C) Parasocial relationship
segments.tr: - C) 파라소셜 관계

segments.src: - D) Cognitive dissonance
segments.tr: - D) 인지 부조화

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 오늘의 용어

segments.src: - **Source effect:** The way a message's persuasiveness changes depending on who delivers it.
segments.tr: - **출처 효과:** 메시지의 설득력이 누가 전달하느냐에 따라 달라지는 현상.

segments.src: - **Source credibility:** How much expertise and trustworthiness an audience sees in a messenger.
segments.tr: - **출처 신뢰도:** 청중이 메시지 전달자에게서 느끼는 전문성과 신뢰성의 정도.

segments.src: - **Match-up hypothesis:** The idea that an endorser is most effective when their image fits the product.
segments.tr: - **매칭 가설:** 보증인은 자신의 이미지가 제품과 어울릴 때 가장 효과적이라는 생각.

segments.src: - **Meaning transfer:** The process by which cultural meanings tied to a celebrity carry over to an endorsed brand.
segments.tr: - **의미 전이:** 유명인과 연결된 문화적 의미가 보증한 브랜드로 옮겨 가는 과정.

segments.src: - **Parasocial relationship:** A one-sided feeling of personal connection with a media figure.
segments.tr: - **파라소셜 관계:** 미디어 인물에 대해 느끼는 일방적인 개인적 유대감.

segments.src: *Answers: Q1 – B.
segments.tr: *정답: Q1 – B.

segments.src: Credibility comes down to whether the source knows the topic (expertise) and whether they're being honest (trustworthiness).
segments.tr: 신뢰도는 출처가 주제를 아는지(전문성)와 솔직한지(신뢰성)에 달려 있다.

segments.src: Q2 – False.
segments.tr: Q2 – 거짓.

segments.src: Fit matters.
segments.tr: 적합성이 중요하다.

segments.src: A famous endorser who doesn't match the product can be less effective than a less famous one who does.
segments.tr: 제품과 맞지 않는 유명 보증인은, 제품과 맞는 덜 유명한 인물보다 효과가 떨어질 수 있다.

segments.src: Q3 – C.
segments.tr: Q3 – C.

segments.src: A parasocial relationship is a one-sided sense of intimacy, and it's a big part of why influencer recommendations can feel like advice from a friend.*
segments.tr: 파라소셜 관계는 일방적인 친밀감이며, 인플루언서의 추천이 친구의 조언처럼 느껴지는 큰 이유 중 하나다.*

zh.title: [消费者心理学 #7] 谁来说可能与说什么同样重要：广告中的信源效应

segments.src: > The same message can persuade more or less depending on who delivers it. We judge a source by expertise, trustworthiness, attractiveness, and whether they "fit" the product.
segments.tr: > 同样的信息，由谁来传达，说服力可能大不相同。我们会从专业性、可信赖性、吸引力，以及发言者是否与产品“契合”来判断一个信源。

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 今日概念

segments.src: Imagine two people telling you a new sunscreen is great.
segments.tr: 试想两个人都告诉你一款新防晒霜很好用。

segments.src: One is a dermatologist.
segments.tr: 一个是皮肤科医生。

segments.src: The other is a stranger in a parking lot.
segments.tr: 另一个是停车场里的陌生人。

segments.src: The words are identical, but you probably trust one more.
segments.tr: 两人的话一字不差，但你大概会更相信前者。

segments.src: Psychologists call this the **source effect**: who delivers a message changes how persuasive it is.
segments.tr: 心理学家把这种现象称为**信源效应**：谁传递信息，会改变信息的说服力。

segments.src: Research going back to Carl Hovland and his colleagues at Yale in the 1950s points to a few main qualities people look for in a source.
segments.tr: 早在20世纪50年代，耶鲁大学的卡尔·霍夫兰（Carl Hovland）及其同事的研究就指出，人们在判断信源时会关注几项主要特质。

segments.src: Credibility.** Credibility has two parts:
segments.tr: 可信度。** 可信度包括两个部分：

segments.src: - **Expertise** asks whether this person knows what they are talking about. A mechanic recommending motor oil carries weight.
segments.tr: - **专业性**：这个人是否真正懂行？推荐机油的技师更有说服力。

segments.src: - **Trustworthiness** asks whether this person is being honest with you. People trust a source more when it seems to have nothing to gain. That's why "I'm not paid to say this" is such a common line, and why a reviewer who points out a product's flaws can come across as *more* believable.
segments.tr: - **可信赖性**：这个人是否对你坦诚？当信源看起来没有任何好处可图时，人们会更信任。这就是为什么“我没有收钱才这么说”是一句很常见的话，也是为什么指出产品缺点的评测者反而可能显得*更*可信。

segments.src: Attractiveness.** This covers more than looks.
segments.tr: 吸引力。** 这不仅指外貌。

segments.src: It includes being likable, being familiar, and seeming similar to you.
segments.tr: 它还包括讨人喜欢、熟悉感，以及是否看起来与你相似。

segments.src: We tend to listen to people we like and people who seem "like us," and sometimes we copy them.
segments.tr: 我们往往更愿意听讨人喜欢的人，或看起来“和我们一样”的人的话，有时甚至会模仿他们。

segments.src: That's part of why everyday-looking actors show up in so many ads.
segments.tr: 这也是为什么许多广告里会出现看起来很普通的演员。

segments.src: Fit (the match-up hypothesis).** A source works best when their image matches the product.
segments.tr: 契合度（匹配假说）。** 当信源的形象与产品相匹配时，效果最好。

segments.src: A star athlete selling sports drinks feels natural.
segments.tr: 一位明星运动员代言运动饮料，会显得很自然。

segments.src: The same athlete selling retirement annuities feels off.
segments.tr: 同一位运动员代言养老年金险，就会让人觉得别扭。

segments.src: Anthropologist Grant McCracken described a related idea called **meaning transfer**: a celebrity carries cultural meanings (toughness, luxury, humor), and an endorsement tries to move those meanings onto the brand.
segments.tr: 人类学家格兰特·麦克拉肯（Grant McCracken）提出了一个相关概念，称为**意义转移**：名人身上承载着某些文化意义（如硬朗、奢华、幽默），代言则试图把这些意义转移到品牌上。

segments.src: If the meanings don't match the product, the transfer falls flat.
segments.tr: 如果这些意义与产品不相符，转移就会失效。

segments.src: They also carry risks: a scandal can drag the brand down with them, and a star who endorses many products can seem less sincere.

segments.src: Influencers often have smaller audiences, but their followers may feel a **parasocial relationship**, a one-sided sense of knowing them personally.
segments.tr: 网红的受众通常较少，但他们的粉丝可能会产生**准社会关系**，即一种单方面的“我很了解这个人”的感觉。

segments.src: That feeling of closeness can make a recommendation feel like advice from a friend.

segments.src: One more twist is the **sleeper effect**.

segments.src: Sometimes a message from a low-credibility source gains persuasive power over time, because people remember the message but forget where it came from.

segments.src: Researchers have found the effect is real but shows up only under fairly specific conditions, so don't count on it as a strategy.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 日常生活中

segments.src: Say you're scrolling TikTok and see a creator with about 80,000 followers raving about a $14 drugstore moisturizer.
segments.tr: 假设你在刷TikTok，看到一位约有8万粉丝的创作者在盛赞一款14美元的药妆保湿霜。

segments.src: She shows her bare skin, mentions she has dry patches like you, and says it beats the $60 department-store cream she used to buy.
segments.tr: 她展示了素颜的皮肤，提到和你一样有干燥斑块，并说这款产品比她以前买的60美元专柜面霜更好用。

segments.src: Several source effects are at work here:
segments.tr: 这里同时起作用的有几种信源效应：

segments.src: - **Similarity:** she has the same skin problem you do, so she feels "like you."
segments.tr: - **相似性：** 她和你有同样的皮肤问题，所以让你觉得“她跟我一样”。

segments.src: - **Perceived honesty:** praising a cheaper product makes her seem less like she's selling something.
segments.tr: - **感知诚实度：** 推荐更便宜的产品，会让她看起来不像在推销。

segments.src: - **Parasocial closeness:** you've watched her morning routine for months, so it feels like a tip from a friend.
segments.tr: - **准社会亲近感：** 你已经看了她几个月的晨间护肤流程，所以这个推荐感觉就像朋友的贴士。

segments.src: Once you see that label, your sense of her trustworthiness may shift a bit.

segments.src: ## 3-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## 三行总结

segments.src: 1. Persuasion depends on the messenger as well as the message. People weigh a source's expertise, trustworthiness, and attractiveness.
segments.tr: 1. 说服力既取决于信息，也取决于传递者。人们会权衡信源的专业性、可信赖性和吸引力。

segments.src: 2. Endorsers work best when their image fits the product (match-up hypothesis), because the celebrity's meaning carries over to the brand.
segments.tr: 2. 当代言人的形象与产品契合（匹配假说）时效果最好，因为名人身上的意义会转移到品牌上。

segments.src: 3. Influencers persuade through closeness and similarity. Disclosure rules like the FTC's exist so consumers know when that closeness is paid for.
segments.tr: 3. 网红依靠亲近感和相似性来说服人。像FTC披露规定这样的制度，就是为了让消费者知道这种亲近感是否是付费换来的。

segments.src: Imagine two people telling you a new sunscreen is great.

segments.src: One is a dermatologist.
segments.tr: एक त्वचा-विशेषज्ञ (डर्मेटोलॉजिस्ट) है।

segments.src: The other is a stranger in a parking lot.
segments.tr: दूसरा पार्किंग लॉट में खड़ा एक अजनबी है।

segments.src: The words are identical, but you probably trust one more.
segments.tr: शब्द एक जैसे हैं, फिर भी आप शायद एक पर ज़्यादा भरोसा करेंगे।

segments.src: Psychologists call this the **source effect**: who delivers a message changes how persuasive it is.
segments.tr: मनोवैज्ञानिक इसे **स्रोत प्रभाव (source effect)** कहते हैं: कौन संदेश दे रहा है, इससे तय होता है कि वह कितना प्रेरक है।

segments.src: Research going back to Carl Hovland and his colleagues at Yale in the 1950s points to a few main qualities people look for in a source.
segments.tr: 1950 के दशक में Yale में Carl Hovland और उनके सहयोगियों से शुरू हुए शोध बताते हैं कि लोग किसी स्रोत में कुछ मुख्य गुण खोजते हैं।

segments.src: Credibility.** Credibility has two parts:
segments.tr: विश्वसनीयता (Credibility).** विश्वसनीयता के दो हिस्से होते हैं:

segments.src: - **Expertise** asks whether this person knows what they are talking about. A mechanic recommending motor oil carries weight.
segments.tr: - **विशेषज्ञता (Expertise)** पूछती है कि क्या यह व्यक्ति जिस विषय पर बोल रहा है उसे सचमुच जानता है। मोटर ऑयल की सिफ़ारिश करने वाले मैकेनिक की बात का वज़न होता है।

segments.src: - **Trustworthiness** asks whether this person is being honest with you. People trust a source more when it seems to have nothing to gain. That's why "I'm not paid to say this" is such a common line, and why a reviewer who points out a product's flaws can come across as *more* believable.
segments.tr: - **भरोसेमंदी (Trustworthiness)** पूछती है कि क्या यह व्यक्ति आपसे ईमानदार है। जब किसी स्रोत को कुछ भी हासिल करने की चाह न दिखे, तो लोग उस पर ज़्यादा भरोसा करते हैं। इसीलिए “मुझे यह कहने के पैसे नहीं मिल रहे” जैसी बात इतनी आम है, और कोई समीक्षक जब किसी उत्पाद की खामियाँ बताता है, तो वह *ज़्यादा* विश्वसनीय लग सकता है।

segments.src: Attractiveness.** This covers more than looks.
segments.tr: आकर्षण (Attractiveness).** यह सिर्फ़ रूप-रंग तक सीमित नहीं है।

segments.src: It includes being likable, being familiar, and seeming similar to you.
segments.tr: इसमें पसंद किया जाना, परिचित लगना, और आपके जैसा दिखना भी शामिल है।

segments.src: We tend to listen to people we like and people who seem "like us," and sometimes we copy them.
segments.tr: हम उन लोगों की बात ज़्यादा सुनते हैं जिन्हें हम पसंद करते हैं, और जो “हमारे जैसे” लगते हैं, और कभी-कभी हम उनकी नकल भी करने लगते हैं।

segments.src: That's part of why everyday-looking actors show up in so many ads.
segments.tr: इसी वजह से रोज़मर्रा की तरह दिखने वाले अभिनेता इतने विज्ञापनों में नज़र आते हैं।

segments.src: Fit (the match-up hypothesis).** A source works best when their image matches the product.
segments.tr: फिट (मेल-मिलान परिकल्पना / match-up hypothesis).** कोई स्रोत तब सबसे अच्छा काम करता है जब उसकी छवि उत्पाद से मेल खाती हो।

segments.src: A star athlete selling sports drinks feels natural.
segments.tr: किसी स्टार एथलीट का स्पोर्ट्स ड्रिंक बेचना स्वाभाविक लगता है।

segments.src: The same athlete selling retirement annuities feels off.
segments.tr: वही एथलीट अगर रिटायरमेंट एन्युइटी बेचे, तो बात बेमेल लगती है।

segments.src: Anthropologist Grant McCracken described a related idea called **meaning transfer**: a celebrity carries cultural meanings (toughness, luxury, humor), and an endorsement tries to move those meanings onto the brand.
segments.tr: मानवविज्ञानी (anthropologist) Grant McCracken ने इससे जुड़ा विचार बताया, जिसे **अर्थ-हस्तांतरण (meaning transfer)** कहते हैं: किसी सेलिब्रिटी के साथ सांस्कृतिक अर्थ जुड़े होते हैं (जैसे दमखम, विलासिता, हास्य), और समर्थन (endorsement) का मकसद उन अर्थों को ब्रांड पर ले जाना होता है।

segments.src: If the meanings don't match the product, the transfer falls flat.
segments.tr: अगर वे अर्थ उत्पाद से मेल नहीं खाते, तो यह हस्तांतरण बेअसर रहता है।

es.title: [Psicología del consumidor #7] Quién lo dice puede importar tanto como lo que dice: efectos de la fuente en la publicidad

segments.src: > The same message can persuade more or less depending on who delivers it. We judge a source by expertise, trustworthiness, attractiveness, and whether they "fit" the product.
segments.tr: > El mismo mensaje puede persuadir más o menos según quién lo transmita. Juzgamos a una fuente por su experiencia, su fiabilidad, su atractivo y si "encaja" con el producto.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Concepto de hoy

segments.src: Imagine two people telling you a new sunscreen is great.
segments.tr: Imagina que dos personas te dicen que un nuevo protector solar es genial.

segments.src: One is a dermatologist.
segments.tr: Una es dermatóloga.

segments.src: The other is a stranger in a parking lot.
segments.tr: La otra es un desconocido en un estacionamiento.

segments.src: The words are identical, but you probably trust one more.
segments.tr: Las palabras son idénticas, pero probablemente confiarías más en una de ellas.

segments.src: Psychologists call this the **source effect**: who delivers a message changes how persuasive it is.
segments.tr: Los psicólogos llaman a esto **efecto de la fuente**: quién transmite un mensaje cambia lo persuasivo que resulta.

segments.src: Research going back to Carl Hovland and his colleagues at Yale in the 1950s points to a few main qualities people look for in a source.
segments.tr: Las investigaciones que se remontan a Carl Hovland y sus colegas de Yale en los años cincuenta señalan algunas cualidades principales que la gente busca en una fuente.

segments.src: Credibility.** Credibility has two parts:
segments.tr: Credibilidad.** La credibilidad tiene dos componentes:

segments.src: - **Expertise** asks whether this person knows what they are talking about. A mechanic recommending motor oil carries weight.
segments.tr: - **La experiencia** pregunta si esta persona sabe de lo que habla. Un mecánico que recomienda aceite de motor tiene peso.

segments.src: - **Trustworthiness** asks whether this person is being honest with you. People trust a source more when it seems to have nothing to gain. That's why "I'm not paid to say this" is such a common line, and why a reviewer who points out a product's flaws can come across as *more* believable.
segments.tr: - **La fiabilidad** pregunta si esta persona es honesta contigo. La gente confía más en una fuente cuando parece no tener nada que ganar. Por eso la frase "no me pagan por decir esto" es tan común, y por qué un crítico que señala los defectos de un producto puede parecer *más* creíble.

segments.src: Attractiveness.** This covers more than looks.
segments.tr: Atractivo.** Esto abarca más que el aspecto físico.

segments.src: It includes being likable, being familiar, and seeming similar to you.
segments.tr: Incluye caer bien, resultar familiar y parecerse a ti.

segments.src: We tend to listen to people we like and people who seem "like us," and sometimes we copy them.
segments.tr: Tendemos a escuchar a las personas que nos gustan y a quienes parecen "como nosotros", y a veces los imitamos.

segments.src: That's part of why everyday-looking actors show up in so many ads.
segments.tr: Por eso aparecen actores de aspecto cotidiano en tantos anuncios.

segments.src: Fit (the match-up hypothesis).** A source works best when their image matches the product.
segments.tr: Ajuste (hipótesis de correspondencia).** Una fuente funciona mejor cuando su imagen encaja con el producto.

segments.src: A star athlete selling sports drinks feels natural.
segments.tr: Un atleta estrella que promociona bebidas deportivas resulta natural.

segments.src: The same athlete selling retirement annuities feels off.
segments.tr: Ese mismo atleta promocionando anualidades para la jubilación resulta fuera de lugar.

segments.src: Anthropologist Grant McCracken described a related idea called **meaning transfer**: a celebrity carries cultural meanings (toughness, luxury, humor), and an endorsement tries to move those meanings onto the brand.
segments.tr: El antropólogo Grant McCracken describió una idea relacionada llamada **transferencia de significado**: una celebridad lleva consigo significados culturales (dureza, lujo, humor), y un respaldo intenta trasladar esos significados a la marca.

segments.src: If the meanings don't match the product, the transfer falls flat.
segments.tr: Si los significados no encajan con el producto, la transferencia fracasa.

segments.src: **Celebrities vs.
segments.tr: **Celebridades frente a

segments.src: influencers.** Celebrities bring instant attention and recognition.
segments.tr: influencers.** Las celebridades aportan atención y reconocimiento inmediatos.

segments.src: They also carry risks: a scandal can drag the brand down with them, and a star who endorses many products can seem less sincere.
segments.tr: También conllevan riesgos: un escándalo puede arrastrar a la marca con ellas, y una estrella que respalda muchos productos puede parecer menos sincera.

segments.src: Influencers often have smaller audiences, but their followers may feel a **parasocial relationship**, a one-sided sense of knowing them personally.
segments.tr: Los influencers suelen tener audiencias más pequeñas, pero sus seguidores pueden sentir una **relación parasocial**, una sensación unilateral de conocerlos personalmente.

segments.src: That feeling of closeness can make a recommendation feel like advice from a friend.
segments.tr: Esa sensación de cercanía puede hacer que una recomendación parezca un consejo de un amigo.

segments.src: One more twist is the **sleeper effect**.
segments.tr: Otro giro es el **efecto durmiente**.

segments.src: Sometimes a message from a low-credibility source gains persuasive power over time, because people remember the message but forget where it came from.
segments.tr: A veces, un mensaje de una fuente de baja credibilidad gana poder persuasivo con el tiempo, porque la gente recuerda el mensaje pero olvida de dónde vino.

segments.src: Researchers have found the effect is real but shows up only under fairly specific conditions, so don't count on it as a strategy.
segments.tr: Los investigadores han comprobado que el efecto es real, pero solo aparece bajo condiciones bastante específicas, así que no lo tomes como estrategia.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## En la vida cotidiana

segments.src: Say you're scrolling TikTok and see a creator with about 80,000 followers raving about a $14 drugstore moisturizer.
segments.tr: Imagina que estás desplazándote por TikTok y ves a una creadora con unos 80 000 seguidores elogiando una crema hidratante de farmacia de 14 dólares.

segments.src: She shows her bare skin, mentions she has dry patches like you, and says it beats the $60 department-store cream she used to buy.
segments.tr: Muestra su piel sin maquillaje, menciona que tiene zonas secas como tú y dice que supera a la crema de 60 dólares de unos grandes almacenes que solía comprar.

segments.src: Several source effects are at work here:
segments.tr: Hay varios efectos de la fuente en juego:

segments.src: - **Similarity:** she has the same skin problem you do, so she feels "like you."
segments.tr: - **Similitud:** tiene el mismo problema de piel que tú, así que te resulta "como tú".

segments.src: - **Perceived honesty:** praising a cheaper product makes her seem less like she's selling something.
segments.tr: - **Honestidad percibida:** elogiar un producto más barato hace que parezca menos que está vendiendo algo.

segments.src: - **Parasocial closeness:** you've watched her morning routine for months, so it feels like a tip from a friend.
segments.tr: - **Cercanía parasocial:** llevas meses viendo su rutina matutina, así que parece un consejo de una amiga.

segments.src: Now look for the small "#ad" or "Paid partnership" label.
segments.tr: Ahora busca la pequeña etiqueta "#ad" o "Colaboración pagada".

segments.tr: Comisión Federal de Comercio (FTC) de EE. UU. exige a los influencers revelar claramente las relaciones materiales con las marcas, como pagos o productos gratuitos.

segments.src: Once you see that label, your sense of her trustworthiness may shift a bit.
segments.tr: Una vez que ves esa etiqueta, tu percepción de su fiabilidad puede cambiar un poco.

segments.src: That's the source effect working in reverse.
segments.tr: Eso es el efecto de la fuente funcionando al revés.

segments.src: The product hasn't changed, but your read on the messenger has.
segments.tr: El producto no ha cambiado, pero tu opinión sobre quien lo transmite sí.

segments.tr: - **الجدارة بالثقة** تسأل: هل هذا الشخص صادق معك؟ يثق الناس بالمصدر أكثر حين يبدو أنه لا يجني شيئًا من كلامه. لهذا تنتشر عبارة «لم أحصل على أي مقابل لقول هذا»، ولهذا قد يبدو المراجع الذي يشير إلى عيوب المنتج أكثر *مصداقية*.

segments.tr: ولهذا يظهر ممثلون يبدون عاديين في كثير من الإعلانات.

segments.src: Anthropologist Grant McCracken described a related idea called **meaning transfer**: a celebrity carries cultural meanings (toughness, luxury, humor), and an endorsement tries to move those meanings onto the brand.

segments.src: They also carry risks: a scandal can drag the brand down with them, and a star who endorses many products can seem less sincere.

fr.title: [Psychologie du consommateur #7] Pourquoi l'identité de celui qui parle compte autant que ce qu'il dit : les effets de source dans la publicité

segments.src: > The same message can persuade more or less depending on who delivers it. We judge a source by expertise, trustworthiness, attractiveness, and whether they "fit" the product.
segments.tr: > Le même message peut persuader plus ou moins selon la personne qui le transmet. Nous jugeons une source selon son expertise, sa crédibilité, son attrait et sa capacité à « coller » au produit.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Concept du jour

segments.src: Imagine two people telling you a new sunscreen is great.
segments.tr: Imaginez deux personnes qui vous disent qu'une nouvelle crème solaire est excellente.

segments.src: One is a dermatologist.
segments.tr: L'une est dermatologue.

segments.src: The other is a stranger in a parking lot.
segments.tr: L'autre est un inconnu sur un parking.

segments.src: The words are identical, but you probably trust one more.
segments.tr: Les mots sont identiques, mais vous ferez probablement davantage confiance à la première.

segments.src: Psychologists call this the **source effect**: who delivers a message changes how persuasive it is.
segments.tr: Les psychologues appellent cela l'**effet de source** : la personne qui transmet un message modifie son pouvoir de persuasion.

segments.src: Research going back to Carl Hovland and his colleagues at Yale in the 1950s points to a few main qualities people look for in a source.
segments.tr: Les recherches remontant à Carl Hovland et à ses collègues de Yale, dans les années 1950, mettent en évidence quelques qualités principales que les gens recherchent chez une source.

segments.src: Credibility.** Credibility has two parts:
segments.tr: Crédibilité.** La crédibilité comporte deux volets :

segments.src: - **Expertise** asks whether this person knows what they are talking about. A mechanic recommending motor oil carries weight.
segments.tr: - **L'expertise** consiste à se demander si cette personne connaît vraiment son sujet. Un mécanicien recommandant une huile moteur a du poids.

segments.src: - **Trustworthiness** asks whether this person is being honest with you. People trust a source more when it seems to have nothing to gain. That's why "I'm not paid to say this" is such a common line, and why a reviewer who points out a product's flaws can come across as *more* believable.
segments.tr: - **L'honnêteté** consiste à se demander si cette personne est sincère avec vous. On fait davantage confiance à une source qui semble n'avoir rien à gagner. C'est pourquoi « Je ne suis pas payé pour dire cela » est une formule si courante, et pourquoi un critique qui souligne les défauts d'un produit peut paraître *plus* crédible.

segments.src: Attractiveness.** This covers more than looks.
segments.tr: Attrait.** Ce concept dépasse la simple apparence.

segments.src: It includes being likable, being familiar, and seeming similar to you.
segments.tr: Il englobe la sympathie, la familiarité et le sentiment de ressembler à son interlocuteur.

segments.src: We tend to listen to people we like and people who seem "like us," and sometimes we copy them.
segments.tr: Nous avons tendance à écouter les personnes que nous aimons et celles qui semblent « comme nous », et parfois nous les imitons.

segments.src: That's part of why everyday-looking actors show up in so many ads.
segments.tr: C'est en partie pour cela que des acteurs à l'allure ordinaire apparaissent dans tant de publicités.

segments.src: Fit (the match-up hypothesis).** A source works best when their image matches the product.
segments.tr: Adéquation (hypothèse du match-up).** Une source est d'autant plus efficace que son image correspond au produit.

segments.src: A star athlete selling sports drinks feels natural.
segments.tr: Une star du sport qui vend des boissons énergétiques semble naturelle.

segments.src: The same athlete selling retirement annuities feels off.
segments.tr: La même athlète qui vend des contrats de retraite paraît déplacée.

segments.src: Anthropologist Grant McCracken described a related idea called **meaning transfer**: a celebrity carries cultural meanings (toughness, luxury, humor), and an endorsement tries to move those meanings onto the brand.
segments.tr: L'anthropologue Grant McCracken a décrit une notion voisine, le **transfert de sens** : une célébrité porte des significations culturelles (la robustesse, le luxe, l'humour), et une campagne de promotion cherche à transférer ces significations vers la marque.

segments.src: If the meanings don't match the product, the transfer falls flat.
segments.tr: Si ces significations ne correspondent pas au produit, le transfert ne fonctionne pas.

segments.tr: influenceurs.** Les célébrités attirent immédiatement l'attention et sont reconnues.

segments.src: They also carry risks: a scandal can drag the brand down with them, and a star who endorses many products can seem less sincere.
segments.tr: Elles comportent aussi des risques : un scandale peut entraîner la marque dans sa chute, et une star qui recommande de nombreux produits peut paraître moins sincère.

segments.tr: Les influenceurs ont souvent des audiences plus restreintes, mais leurs abonnés peuvent ressentir une **relation parasociale**, un sentiment unilatéral de les connaître personnellement.

segments.src: That feeling of closeness can make a recommendation feel like advice from a friend.

segments.src: Sometimes a message from a low-credibility source gains persuasive power over time, because people remember the message but forget where it came from.
segments.tr: Parfois, un message émanant d'une source peu crédible gagne en pouvoir de persuasion avec le temps, parce que les gens retiennent le message mais oublient d'où il vient.

pt.title: [Consumer Psychology #7] Por que quem diz pode importar tanto quanto o que se diz: efeitos da fonte na publicidade

segments.src: > The same message can persuade more or less depending on who delivers it. We judge a source by expertise, trustworthiness, attractiveness, and whether they "fit" the product.
segments.tr: > A mesma mensagem pode persuadir mais ou menos dependendo de quem a transmite. Julgamos uma fonte pela expertise, pela confiabilidade, pela atratividade e por quanto ela “se encaixa” no produto.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Conceito de hoje

segments.src: Imagine two people telling you a new sunscreen is great.
segments.tr: Imagine duas pessoas dizendo que um novo protetor solar é ótimo.

segments.src: One is a dermatologist.
segments.tr: Uma é dermatologista.

segments.src: The other is a stranger in a parking lot.
segments.tr: A outra é um desconhecido em um estacionamento.

segments.src: The words are identical, but you probably trust one more.
segments.tr: As palavras são idênticas, mas você provavelmente confia mais em uma delas.

segments.src: Psychologists call this the **source effect**: who delivers a message changes how persuasive it is.
segments.tr: Os psicólogos chamam isso de **efeito da fonte**: quem transmite uma mensagem muda o quanto ela é persuasiva.

segments.src: Research going back to Carl Hovland and his colleagues at Yale in the 1950s points to a few main qualities people look for in a source.
segments.tr: Pesquisas que remontam a Carl Hovland e seus colegas de Yale, na década de 1950, apontam algumas qualidades principais que as pessoas procuram em uma fonte.

segments.src: Credibility.** Credibility has two parts:
segments.tr: Credibilidade.** A credibilidade tem duas partes:

segments.src: - **Expertise** asks whether this person knows what they are talking about. A mechanic recommending motor oil carries weight.
segments.tr: - **Expertise** pergunta se essa pessoa entende do assunto. Um mecânico recomendando óleo de motor tem peso.

segments.src: - **Trustworthiness** asks whether this person is being honest with you. People trust a source more when it seems to have nothing to gain. That's why "I'm not paid to say this" is such a common line, and why a reviewer who points out a product's flaws can come across as *more* believable.
segments.tr: - **Confiabilidade** pergunta se essa pessoa está sendo honesta com você. As pessoas confiam mais em uma fonte quando ela parece não ter nada a ganhar. Por isso “não estou sendo pago para dizer isso” é uma frase tão comum, e por que um avaliador que aponta os defeitos de um produto pode parecer *ainda mais* crível.

segments.src: Attractiveness.** This covers more than looks.
segments.tr: Atratividade.** Isso vai além da aparência.

segments.src: It includes being likable, being familiar, and seeming similar to you.
segments.tr: Inclui ser simpático, ser familiar e parecer semelhante a você.

segments.src: We tend to listen to people we like and people who seem "like us," and sometimes we copy them.
segments.tr: Tendemos a ouvir pessoas de que gostamos e pessoas que parecem “como nós”, e às vezes as imitamos.

segments.src: That's part of why everyday-looking actors show up in so many ads.
segments.tr: Isso explica, em parte, por que atores de aparência comum aparecem em tantos anúncios.

segments.src: Fit (the match-up hypothesis).** A source works best when their image matches the product.
segments.tr: Adequação (hipótese de match-up).** Uma fonte funciona melhor quando sua imagem combina com o produto.

segments.src: A star athlete selling sports drinks feels natural.
segments.tr: Um atleta de destaque vendendo bebidas esportivas parece natural.

segments.src: The same athlete selling retirement annuities feels off.
segments.tr: O mesmo atleta vendendo previdência privada soa deslocado.

segments.src: Anthropologist Grant McCracken described a related idea called **meaning transfer**: a celebrity carries cultural meanings (toughness, luxury, humor), and an endorsement tries to move those meanings onto the brand.
segments.tr: Em um estudo de antropologia, Grant McCracken descreveu uma ideia relacionada chamada **transferência de significado**: uma celebridade carrega significados culturais (força, luxo, humor), e um endosso tenta transferir esses significados para a marca.

segments.src: If the meanings don't match the product, the transfer falls flat.
segments.tr: Se os significados não combinam com o produto, a transferência não funciona.

segments.src: **Celebrities vs.
segments.tr: **Celebridades x

segments.src: influencers.** Celebrities bring instant attention and recognition.
segments.tr: influenciadores.** Celebridades trazem atenção e reconhecimento imediatos.

segments.src: They also carry risks: a scandal can drag the brand down with them, and a star who endorses many products can seem less sincere.
segments.tr: Elas também carregam riscos: um escândalo pode arrastar a marca junto, e uma estrela que endossa muitos produtos pode parecer menos sincera.

segments.src: Influencers often have smaller audiences, but their followers may feel a **parasocial relationship**, a one-sided sense of knowing them personally.
segments.tr: Influenciadores costumam ter audiências menores, mas seus seguidores podem sentir uma **relação parassocial**, uma sensação unilateral de conhecer a pessoa pessoalmente.

segments.src: That feeling of closeness can make a recommendation feel like advice from a friend.
segments.tr: Essa sensação de proximidade pode fazer uma recomendação parecer um conselho de um amigo.

segments.src: One more twist is the **sleeper effect**.
segments.tr: Outra reviravolta é o **efeito sleeper**.

segments.src: Sometimes a message from a low-credibility source gains persuasive power over time, because people remember the message but forget where it came from.
segments.tr: Às vezes, uma mensagem vinda de uma fonte de baixa credibilidade ganha poder de persuasão com o tempo, porque as pessoas lembram da mensagem, mas esquecem de onde ela veio.

segments.src: Researchers have found the effect is real but shows up only under fairly specific conditions, so don't count on it as a strategy.
segments.tr: Pesquisadores constataram que o efeito é real, mas aparece apenas em condições bastante específicas, então não conte com ele como estratégia.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## No dia a dia

segments.src: Say you're scrolling TikTok and see a creator with about 80,000 followers raving about a $14 drugstore moisturizer.
segments.tr: Imagine que você está rolando o TikTok e vê uma criadora com cerca de 80 mil seguidores elogiando um hidratante de farmácia de $14.

segments.src: She shows her bare skin, mentions she has dry patches like you, and says it beats the $60 department-store cream she used to buy.
segments.tr: Ela mostra a pele sem maquiagem, comenta que tem manchas secas como as suas e diz que ele é melhor do que o creme de $60 de loja de departamento que costumava comprar.

segments.src: Several source effects are at work here:
segments.tr: Vários efeitos da fonte estão em jogo aqui:

segments.src: - **Similarity:** she has the same skin problem you do, so she feels "like you."
segments.tr: - **Semelhança:** ela tem o mesmo problema de pele que você, então parece “como você”.

segments.src: - **Perceived honesty:** praising a cheaper product makes her seem less like she's selling something.
segments.tr: - **Honestidade percebida:** elogiar um produto mais barato faz com que ela pareça menos interessada em vender algo.

segments.src: - **Parasocial closeness:** you've watched her morning routine for months, so it feels like a tip from a friend.
segments.tr: - **Proximidade parassocial:** você acompanha a rotina matinal dela há meses, então parece uma dica de amiga.

segments.src: Now look for the small "#ad" or "Paid partnership" label.
segments.tr: Agora procure o pequeno rótulo “#ad” ou “Parceria paga”.

segments.src: The U.S.
segments.tr: A

segments.src: Federal Trade Commission (FTC) requires influencers to clearly disclose material connections to brands, such as payment or free products.
segments.tr: Comissão Federal de Comércio (FTC) dos EUA exige que influenciadores divulguem com clareza vínculos relevantes com marcas, como pagamento ou produtos recebidos gratuitamente.

segments.src: Once you see that label, your sense of her trustworthiness may shift a bit.
segments.tr: Depois de ver esse rótulo, sua percepção sobre a confiabilidade dela pode mudar um pouco.

segments.src: That's the source effect working in reverse.
segments.tr: Isso é o efeito da fonte funcionando ao contrário.

segments.src: The product hasn't changed, but your read on the messenger has.
segments.tr: O produto não mudou, mas sua leitura sobre quem transmite a mensagem, sim.

segments.src: ## 3-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## Resumo em 3 linhas

segments.src: 1. Persuasion depends on the messenger as well as the message. People weigh a source's expertise, trustworthiness, and attractiveness.
segments.tr: 1. A persuasão depende de quem transmite tanto quanto da mensagem. As pessoas avaliam a expertise, a confiabilidade e a atratividade de uma fonte.

segments.src: 2. Endorsers work best when their image fits the product (match-up hypothesis), because the celebrity's meaning carries over to the brand.
segments.tr: 2. Endossantes funcionam melhor quando sua imagem combina com o produto (hipótese de match-up), porque o significado da celebridade se transfere para a marca.

segments.src: 3. Influencers persuade through closeness and similarity. Disclosure rules like the FTC's exist so consumers know when that closeness is paid for.
segments.tr: 3. Influenciadores persuadem por meio de proximidade e semelhança. Regras de divulgação, como as da FTC, existem para que os consumidores saibam quando essa proximidade é paga.

ja.title: [消費者心理学 #7] なぜ「何を言うか」だけでなく「誰が言うか」も重要なのか：広告における情報源効果

segments.src: > The same message can persuade more or less depending on who delivers it. We judge a source by expertise, trustworthiness, attractiveness, and whether they "fit" the product.
segments.tr: > 同じメッセージでも、誰が伝えるかによって説得力は大きく変わります。人は情報源を、専門性・誠実さ・魅力、そして製品に「合っているか」で判断します。

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 今日のコンセプト

segments.src: Imagine two people telling you a new sunscreen is great.
segments.tr: 新しい日焼け止めが素晴らしいと、二人の人があなたに話しているところを想像してみてください。

segments.src: One is a dermatologist.
segments.tr: 一人は皮膚科医です。

segments.src: The other is a stranger in a parking lot.
segments.tr: もう一人は駐車場で出会った見知らぬ人です。

segments.src: The words are identical, but you probably trust one more.
segments.tr: 言葉はまったく同じですが、おそらく前者の方を信頼するでしょう。

segments.src: Psychologists call this the **source effect**: who delivers a message changes how persuasive it is.
segments.tr: 心理学ではこれを**情報源効果**と呼びます。誰が伝えるかによって、メッセージの説得力が変わるということです。

segments.src: Research going back to Carl Hovland and his colleagues at Yale in the 1950s points to a few main qualities people look for in a source.
segments.tr: 1950年代にイェール大学のカール・ホブランドとその同僚たちが行った研究以来、人が情報源に求める主な特性がいくつか明らかになっています。

segments.src: Credibility.** Credibility has two parts:
segments.tr: **信頼性。** 信頼性は2つの部分から成ります:

segments.src: - **Expertise** asks whether this person knows what they are talking about. A mechanic recommending motor oil carries weight.
segments.tr: - **専門性**は、その人が話している内容を本当に理解しているかどうかを問うものです。エンジンオイルを勧める整備士の言葉には重みがあります。

segments.src: - **Trustworthiness** asks whether this person is being honest with you. People trust a source more when it seems to have nothing to gain. That's why "I'm not paid to say this" is such a common line, and why a reviewer who points out a product's flaws can come across as *more* believable.
segments.tr: - **誠実さ**は、その人があなたに対して正直であるかどうかを問うものです。得るものが何もないように見える情報源ほど、人は信頼します。だからこそ「お金をもらって言っているわけではない」という言い回しがよく使われ、製品の欠点を指摘するレビュアーが、かえって*より*信用できるように見えることがあるのです。

segments.src: Attractiveness.** This covers more than looks.
segments.tr: **魅力。** これは見た目だけにとどまりません。

segments.src: It includes being likable, being familiar, and seeming similar to you.
segments.tr: 好感が持てること、親しみやすいこと、自分と似ているように見えることも含まれます。

segments.src: We tend to listen to people we like and people who seem "like us," and sometimes we copy them.
segments.tr: 人は好きな人や「自分たちに近い」と感じる人の話に耳を傾けやすく、時にはその人を真似することもあります。

segments.src: That's part of why everyday-looking actors show up in so many ads.
segments.tr: 日常的な雰囲気の俳優が多くの広告に登場するのも、それが一因です。

segments.src: Fit (the match-up hypothesis).** A source works best when their image matches the product.
segments.tr: **適合性（マッチアップ仮説）。** 情報源は、そのイメージが製品と合っているときに最も効果的に働きます。

segments.src: A star athlete selling sports drinks feels natural.
segments.tr: スポーツドリンクを売るトップアスリートは自然に感じられます。

segments.src: The same athlete selling retirement annuities feels off.
segments.tr: 一方で、同じアスリートが退職年金商品を売っていると違和感があります。

segments.src: Anthropologist Grant McCracken described a related idea called **meaning transfer**: a celebrity carries cultural meanings (toughness, luxury, humor), and an endorsement tries to move those meanings onto the brand.
segments.tr: 人類学者のグラント・マクラッケンは、関連する考え方として**意味の移転**を提唱しました。有名人は文化的な意味（タフさ、高級感、ユーモアなど）をまとっており、広告塔の起用はその意味をブランドに移そうとするものだというのです。

segments.src: If the meanings don't match the product, the transfer falls flat.
segments.tr: その意味が製品と合わなければ、移転はうまくいきません。

segments.src: **Celebrities vs.
segments.tr: **有名人 vs.

segments.src: influencers.** Celebrities bring instant attention and recognition.
segments.tr: インフルエンサー。** 有名人は即座の注目と認知度をもたらします。

segments.src: They also carry risks: a scandal can drag the brand down with them, and a star who endorses many products can seem less sincere.
segments.tr: 一方でリスクもあります。スキャンダルが起きれば、ブランドも一緒に傷つく可能性がありますし、多くの製品を推薦する有名人は誠実さに欠けるように見えることがあります。

segments.src: Influencers often have smaller audiences, but their followers may feel a **parasocial relationship**, a one-sided sense of knowing them personally.
segments.tr: インフルエンサーは一般に観客数が少ないものの、フォロワーは**パラソーシャル関係**、つまり相手を個人的によく知っているような一方的な感覚を抱くことがあります。

segments.src: That feeling of closeness can make a recommendation feel like advice from a friend.
segments.tr: その親近感があるため、推薦が友人からのアドバイスのように感じられることがあります。

segments.src: One more twist is the **sleeper effect**.
segments.tr: さらにもう一つのひねりが**スリーパー効果**です。

segments.src: Sometimes a message from a low-credibility source gains persuasive power over time, because people remember the message but forget where it came from.
segments.tr: 信頼性の低い情報源からのメッセージが、時間の経過とともに説得力を増すことがあります。人はメッセージは覚えていても、その出所を忘れてしまうからです。

segments.src: Researchers have found the effect is real but shows up only under fairly specific conditions, so don't count on it as a strategy.
segments.tr: 研究者はこの効果が実在することを確認していますが、かなり特定の条件下でしか現れないため、戦略として当てにしないようにしましょう。

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 日常生活では

segments.src: Say you're scrolling TikTok and see a creator with about 80,000 followers raving about a $14 drugstore moisturizer.
segments.tr: TikTokをスクロールしていて、約8万人のフォロワーを持つクリエイターが14ドルのドラッグストアの保湿クリームを絶賛しているのを見たとします。

segments.src: She shows her bare skin, mentions she has dry patches like you, and says it beats the $60 department-store cream she used to buy.
segments.tr: 彼女は素肌を見せ、あなたと同じように乾燥でかさつく部分があると話し、以前買っていた60ドルのデパートのクリームより良いと言います。

segments.src: Several source effects are at work here:
segments.tr: ここでは、いくつかの情報源効果が同時に働いています:

segments.src: - **Similarity:** she has the same skin problem you do, so she feels "like you."
segments.tr: - **類似性:** 彼女はあなたと同じ肌の悩みを抱えているので、「自分に近い人」だと感じられます。

segments.src: - **Perceived honesty:** praising a cheaper product makes her seem less like she's selling something.
segments.tr: - **感じられる誠実さ:** より安い製品を褒めることで、彼女は何かを売り込んでいるようには見えにくくなります。

segments.src: - **Parasocial closeness:** you've watched her morning routine for months, so it feels like a tip from a friend.
segments.tr: - **パラソーシャルな親近感:** 何か月も彼女の朝のルーティンを見てきたので、友人からのちょっとしたアドバイスのように感じられます。

segments.src: Now look for the small "#ad" or "Paid partnership" label.
segments.tr: 次に、小さな「#ad」や「Paid partnership」のラベルを探してみてください。

segments.src: The U.S.
segments.tr: アメリカの

segments.src: Federal Trade Commission (FTC) requires influencers to clearly disclose material connections to brands, such as payment or free products.
segments.tr: 連邦取引委員会（FTC）は、インフルエンサーに対し、支払いや無償提供など、ブランドとの重要な関係を明確に開示することを求めています。

segments.src: Once you see that label, your sense of her trustworthiness may shift a bit.
segments.tr: そのラベルに気づくと、彼女の信頼性に対する感覚が少し変わるかもしれません。

segments.src: That's the source effect working in reverse.
segments.tr: これは情報源効果が逆方向に働いている例です。

segments.src: The product hasn't changed, but your read on the messenger has.
segments.tr: 製品は変わっていませんが、メッセンジャーに対するあなたの見方が変わったのです。

segments.src: ## 3-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## 3行まとめ

segments.tr: 1. 説得は、メッセージだけでなく伝える人にも左右されます。人は情報源の専門性・誠実さ・魅力を比べて判断します。

de.title: [Consumer Psychology #7] Warum wer etwas sagt genauso wichtig sein kann wie das, was gesagt wird: Quelleneffekte in der Werbung

segments.src: > The same message can persuade more or less depending on who delivers it. We judge a source by expertise, trustworthiness, attractiveness, and whether they "fit" the product.
segments.tr: > Dieselbe Botschaft kann je nachdem, wer sie überbringt, mehr oder weniger überzeugen. Wir beurteilen eine Quelle nach Fachkompetenz, Vertrauenswürdigkeit, Attraktivität und danach, ob sie zum Produkt „passt“.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Das heutige Konzept

segments.src: Imagine two people telling you a new sunscreen is great.
segments.tr: Stell dir vor, zwei Personen sagen dir, dass ein neues Sonnenschutzmittel toll ist.

segments.src: One is a dermatologist.
segments.tr: Die eine ist Dermatologin.

segments.src: The other is a stranger in a parking lot.
segments.tr: Die andere ist eine Fremde auf einem Parkplatz.

segments.src: The words are identical, but you probably trust one more.
segments.tr: Die Worte sind identisch, aber du vertraust wahrscheinlich eher der Ersten.

segments.src: Psychologists call this the **source effect**: who delivers a message changes how persuasive it is.
segments.tr: Psychologen nennen das den **Quelleneffekt**: Wer eine Botschaft überbringt, verändert, wie überzeugend sie ist.

segments.src: Research going back to Carl Hovland and his colleagues at Yale in the 1950s points to a few main qualities people look for in a source.
segments.tr: Forschungen seit Carl Hovland und seinen Kolleginnen und Kollegen in Yale in den 1950er-Jahren zeigen einige zentrale Eigenschaften, auf die Menschen bei einer Quelle achten.

segments.src: Credibility.** Credibility has two parts:
segments.tr: Glaubwürdigkeit.** Glaubwürdigkeit hat zwei Teile:

segments.src: - **Expertise** asks whether this person knows what they are talking about. A mechanic recommending motor oil carries weight.
segments.tr: - **Fachkompetenz** fragt, ob diese Person weiß, wovon sie spricht. Ein Mechaniker, der Motoröl empfiehlt, hat Gewicht.

segments.src: - **Trustworthiness** asks whether this person is being honest with you. People trust a source more when it seems to have nothing to gain. That's why "I'm not paid to say this" is such a common line, and why a reviewer who points out a product's flaws can come across as *more* believable.
segments.tr: - **Vertrauenswürdigkeit** fragt, ob diese Person ehrlich zu dir ist. Menschen vertrauen einer Quelle mehr, wenn sie offenbar nichts zu gewinnen hat. Deshalb ist „Ich werde dafür nicht bezahlt“ eine so verbreitete Aussage, und deshalb kann ein Tester, der die Mängel eines Produkts benennt, *glaubwürdiger* wirken.

segments.src: Attractiveness.** This covers more than looks.
segments.tr: Attraktivität.** Das umfasst mehr als das Aussehen.

segments.src: It includes being likable, being familiar, and seeming similar to you.
segments.tr: Dazu gehören Sympathie, Vertrautheit und das Gefühl, dir ähnlich zu sein.

segments.src: We tend to listen to people we like and people who seem "like us," and sometimes we copy them.
segments.tr: Wir hören eher auf Menschen, die wir mögen, und auf Menschen, die „wie wir“ wirken, und manchmal ahmen wir sie nach.

segments.src: That's part of why everyday-looking actors show up in so many ads.
segments.tr: Deshalb tauchen in so vielen Werbespots alltäglich wirkende Schauspielerinnen und Schauspieler auf.

segments.src: Fit (the match-up hypothesis).** A source works best when their image matches the product.
segments.tr: Passung (Match-up-Hypothese).** Eine Quelle wirkt am besten, wenn ihr Image zum Produkt passt.

segments.src: A star athlete selling sports drinks feels natural.
segments.tr: Ein Profisportler, der Sportgetränke bewirbt, wirkt natürlich.

segments.src: The same athlete selling retirement annuities feels off.
segments.tr: Derselbe Sportler, der Rentenversicherungen bewirbt, wirkt unpassend.

segments.src: Anthropologist Grant McCracken described a related idea called **meaning transfer**: a celebrity carries cultural meanings (toughness, luxury, humor), and an endorsement tries to move those meanings onto the brand.
segments.tr: Der Anthropologe Grant McCracken beschrieb eine verwandte Idee namens **Bedeutungstransfer**: Ein Promi trägt kulturelle Bedeutungen (Härte, Luxus, Humor) in sich, und ein Testimonial versucht, diese Bedeutungen auf die Marke zu übertragen.

segments.src: If the meanings don't match the product, the transfer falls flat.
segments.tr: Passen die Bedeutungen nicht zum Produkt, verpufft der Transfer.

segments.src: **Celebrities vs.
segments.tr: **Promis vs.

segments.src: influencers.** Celebrities bring instant attention and recognition.
segments.tr: Influencer.** Promis bringen sofortige Aufmerksamkeit und Bekanntheit.

segments.src: They also carry risks: a scandal can drag the brand down with them, and a star who endorses many products can seem less sincere.
segments.tr: Sie bergen aber auch Risiken: Ein Skandal kann die Marke mit nach unten ziehen, und ein Star, der viele Produkte bewirbt, kann unaufrichtig wirken.

segments.src: Influencers often have smaller audiences, but their followers may feel a **parasocial relationship**, a one-sided sense of knowing them personally.
segments.tr: Influencer haben oft kleinere Publika, doch ihre Follower können eine **parasoziale Beziehung** empfinden, also das einseitige Gefühl, sie persönlich zu kennen.

segments.src: That feeling of closeness can make a recommendation feel like advice from a friend.
segments.tr: Dieses Gefühl der Nähe kann eine Empfehlung wie einen Rat von einer Freundin oder einem Freund wirken lassen.

segments.src: One more twist is the **sleeper effect**.
segments.tr: Eine weitere Wendung ist der **Sleeper-Effekt**.

segments.src: Sometimes a message from a low-credibility source gains persuasive power over time, because people remember the message but forget where it came from.
segments.tr: Manchmal gewinnt eine Botschaft einer wenig glaubwürdigen Quelle mit der Zeit an Überzeugungskraft, weil Menschen sich an die Botschaft erinnern, die Quelle aber vergessen.

segments.src: Researchers have found the effect is real but shows up only under fairly specific conditions, so don't count on it as a strategy.
segments.tr: Die Forschung hat gezeigt, dass der Effekt real ist, aber nur unter ziemlich spezifischen Bedingungen auftritt. Verlass dich also nicht darauf als Strategie.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Im Alltag

segments.src: Say you're scrolling TikTok and see a creator with about 80,000 followers raving about a $14 drugstore moisturizer.
segments.tr: Angenommen, du scrollst durch TikTok und siehst eine Creatorin mit etwa 80.000 Followern, die sich begeistert über eine 14-Dollar-Feuchtigkeitscreme aus der Drogerie äußert.

segments.src: She shows her bare skin, mentions she has dry patches like you, and says it beats the $60 department-store cream she used to buy.
segments.tr: Sie zeigt ihre nackte Haut, erwähnt, dass sie wie du trockene Stellen hat, und sagt, dass die Creme die 60-Dollar-Creme aus dem Kaufhaus schlägt, die sie früher gekauft hat.

segments.src: Several source effects are at work here:
segments.tr: Hier sind mehrere Quelleneffekte am Werk:

segments.src: - **Similarity:** she has the same skin problem you do, so she feels "like you."
segments.tr: - **Ähnlichkeit:** Sie hat dasselbe Hautproblem wie du, also wirkt sie „wie du“.

segments.src: - **Perceived honesty:** praising a cheaper product makes her seem less like she's selling something.
segments.tr: - **Wahrgenommene Ehrlichkeit:** Wer ein günstigeres Produkt lobt, wirkt weniger, als wolle er etwas verkaufen.

segments.src: - **Parasocial closeness:** you've watched her morning routine for months, so it feels like a tip from a friend.
segments.tr: - **Parasoziale Nähe:** Du siehst ihre Morgenroutine seit Monaten, deshalb fühlt es sich an wie ein Tipp von einer Freundin.

segments.src: Now look for the small "#ad" or "Paid partnership" label.
segments.tr: Achte nun auf das kleine Label „#ad“ oder „Bezahlte Partnerschaft“.

segments.src: The U.S.
segments.tr: Die U.S.

segments.src: Federal Trade Commission (FTC) requires influencers to clearly disclose material connections to brands, such as payment or free products.
segments.tr: Federal Trade Commission (FTC) verlangt von Influencern, wesentliche Verbindungen zu Marken klar offenzulegen, etwa Bezahlung oder kostenlose Produkte.

segments.src: Once you see that label, your sense of her trustworthiness may shift a bit.
segments.tr: Sobald du dieses Label siehst, kann sich deine Einschätzung ihrer Vertrauenswürdigkeit etwas verschieben.

segments.src: That's the source effect working in reverse.
segments.tr: Das ist der Quelleneffekt, der rückwärts wirkt.

segments.src: The product hasn't changed, but your read on the messenger has.
segments.tr: Das Produkt hat sich nicht verändert, aber deine Einschätzung des Überbringers schon.

segments.src: ## 3-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## Zusammenfassung in 3 Zeilen

segments.src: 1. Persuasion depends on the messenger as well as the message. People weigh a source's expertise, trustworthiness, and attractiveness.
segments.tr: 1. Überzeugung hängt ebenso vom Überbringer wie von der Botschaft ab. Menschen wägen Fachkompetenz, Vertrauenswürdigkeit und Attraktivität einer Quelle ab.

segments.src: 2. Endorsers work best when their image fits the product (match-up hypothesis), because the celebrity's meaning carries over to the brand.
segments.tr: 2. Testimonials wirken am besten, wenn ihr Image zum Produkt passt (Match-up-Hypothese), weil die Bedeutung des Promis auf die Marke übergeht.

segments.src: 3. Influencers persuade through closeness and similarity. Disclosure rules like the FTC's exist so consumers know when that closeness is paid for.
segments.tr: 3. Influencer überzeugen über Nähe und Ähnlichkeit. Offenlegungspflichten wie die der FTC gibt es, damit Verbraucherinnen und Verbraucher wissen, wann diese Nähe bezahlt ist.

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Begriffe des Tages

segments.src: - **Source effect:** The way a message's persuasiveness changes depending on who delivers it.
segments.tr: - **Quelleneffekt:** Die Art, wie sich die Überzeugungskraft einer Botschaft je nach Überbringer verändert.

segments.src: - **Source credibility:** How much expertise and trustworthiness an audience sees in a messenger.
segments.tr: - **Glaubwürdigkeit der Quelle:** Wie viel Fachkompetenz und Vertrauenswürdigkeit das Publikum einem Überbringer zuschreibt.

segments.src: - **Match-up hypothesis:** The idea that an endorser is most effective when their image fits the product.
segments.tr: - **Match-up-Hypothese:** Die Annahme, dass ein Testimonial am wirksamsten ist, wenn sein Image zum Produkt passt.

segments.src: - **Meaning transfer:** The process by which cultural meanings tied to a celebrity carry over to an endorsed brand.
segments.tr: - **Bedeutungstransfer:** Der Prozess, bei dem kulturelle Bedeutungen eines Promis auf die beworbene Marke übergehen.

segments.src: - **Parasocial relationship:** A one-sided feeling of personal connection with a media figure.
segments.tr: - **Parasoziale Beziehung:** Ein einseitiges Gefühl persönlicher Verbundenheit mit einer Medienfigur.

segments.src: *Answers: Q1 – B.
segments.tr: *Lösungen: F1 – B.

segments.src: Credibility comes down to whether the source knows the topic (expertise) and whether they're being honest (trustworthiness).
segments.tr: Glaubwürdigkeit hängt davon ab, ob die Quelle sich mit dem Thema auskennt (Fachkompetenz) und ob sie ehrlich ist (Vertrauenswürdigkeit).

segments.tr: F2 – Falsch.

segments.tr: Passung zählt.

segments.src: A famous endorser who doesn't match the product can be less effective than a less famous one who does.
segments.tr: Ein bekannter Testimonial-Geber, der nicht zum Produkt passt, kann weniger wirksam sein als ein weniger bekannter, der passt.

segments.src: Q3 – C.
segments.tr: F3 – C.

vi.title: [Consumer Psychology #7] Vì sao người nói cũng quan trọng không kém điều được nói: Hiệu ứng nguồn trong quảng cáo

segments.src: > The same message can persuade more or less depending on who delivers it. We judge a source by expertise, trustworthiness, attractiveness, and whether they "fit" the product.
segments.tr: > Cùng một thông điệp có thể thuyết phục nhiều hay ít tùy thuộc vào người truyền đạt. Chúng ta đánh giá nguồn thông tin qua chuyên môn, mức độ đáng tin cậy, sức hấp dẫn và việc họ có "phù hợp" với sản phẩm hay không.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Khái niệm hôm nay

segments.src: Imagine two people telling you a new sunscreen is great.
segments.tr: Hãy tưởng tượng có hai người cùng nói với bạn rằng một loại kem chống nắng mới rất tốt.

segments.src: One is a dermatologist.
segments.tr: Một người là bác sĩ da liễu.

segments.src: The other is a stranger in a parking lot.
segments.tr: Người kia là một người lạ ở bãi đỗ xe.

segments.src: The words are identical, but you probably trust one more.
segments.tr: Lời nói giống hệt nhau, nhưng có lẽ bạn sẽ tin người thứ nhất hơn.

segments.src: Psychologists call this the **source effect**: who delivers a message changes how persuasive it is.
segments.tr: Các nhà tâm lý học gọi đây là **hiệu ứng nguồn**: ai là người truyền đạt thông điệp sẽ làm thay đổi sức thuyết phục của nó.

segments.src: Research going back to Carl Hovland and his colleagues at Yale in the 1950s points to a few main qualities people look for in a source.
segments.tr: Nghiên cứu từ thời Carl Hovland và các cộng sự của ông tại Yale vào những năm 1950 chỉ ra một vài phẩm chất chính mà con người tìm kiếm ở một nguồn thông tin.

segments.src: Credibility.** Credibility has two parts:
segments.tr: Độ tin cậy.** Độ tin cậy gồm hai phần:

segments.src: - **Expertise** asks whether this person knows what they are talking about. A mechanic recommending motor oil carries weight.
segments.tr: - **Chuyên môn** xét xem người này có thực sự hiểu điều họ đang nói hay không. Một thợ sửa xe giới thiệu dầu nhớt thì có sức nặng.

segments.src: - **Trustworthiness** asks whether this person is being honest with you. People trust a source more when it seems to have nothing to gain. That's why "I'm not paid to say this" is such a common line, and why a reviewer who points out a product's flaws can come across as *more* believable.
segments.tr: - **Tính trung thực** xét xem người này có thành thật với bạn hay không. Người ta tin một nguồn hơn khi nguồn đó dường như chẳng có gì để được lợi. Đó là lý do câu "tôi không được trả tiền để nói điều này" rất phổ biến, và vì sao một người đánh giá chỉ ra nhược điểm của sản phẩm lại có thể nghe đáng tin *hơn*.

segments.src: Attractiveness.** This covers more than looks.
segments.tr: Sức hấp dẫn.** Điều này không chỉ là ngoại hình.

segments.src: It includes being likable, being familiar, and seeming similar to you.
segments.tr: Nó bao gồm việc được yêu mến, quen thuộc và trông giống bạn.

segments.src: We tend to listen to people we like and people who seem "like us," and sometimes we copy them.
segments.tr: Chúng ta có xu hướng lắng nghe những người mình thích và những người có vẻ "giống mình", và đôi khi làm theo họ.

segments.src: That's part of why everyday-looking actors show up in so many ads.
segments.tr: Đó là một phần lý do vì sao những diễn viên có vẻ ngoài bình dị xuất hiện trong rất nhiều quảng cáo.

segments.src: Fit (the match-up hypothesis).** A source works best when their image matches the product.
segments.tr: Sự phù hợp (giả thuyết ghép đôi).** Một nguồn hoạt động hiệu quả nhất khi hình ảnh của họ khớp với sản phẩm.

segments.src: A star athlete selling sports drinks feels natural.
segments.tr: Một vận động viên ngôi sao quảng cáo đồ uống thể thao nghe rất tự nhiên.

segments.src: The same athlete selling retirement annuities feels off.
segments.tr: Cùng vận động viên đó quảng cáo quỹ hưu trí thì nghe lại gượng gạo.

segments.src: Anthropologist Grant McCracken described a related idea called **meaning transfer**: a celebrity carries cultural meanings (toughness, luxury, humor), and an endorsement tries to move those meanings onto the brand.
segments.tr: Nhà nhân học Grant McCracken mô tả một ý tưởng liên quan gọi là **chuyển giao ý nghĩa**: người nổi tiếng mang theo các ý nghĩa văn hóa (sự mạnh mẽ, sang trọng, hài hước), và việc chứng thực sản phẩm cố gắng chuyển những ý nghĩa đó sang thương hiệu.

segments.src: If the meanings don't match the product, the transfer falls flat.
segments.tr: Nếu các ý nghĩa không khớp với sản phẩm, việc chuyển giao sẽ thất bại.

segments.src: **Celebrities vs.
segments.tr: **Người nổi tiếng so với

segments.src: influencers.** Celebrities bring instant attention and recognition.
segments.tr: người có ảnh hưởng (influencer).** Người nổi tiếng mang lại sự chú ý và nhận diện ngay lập tức.

segments.src: They also carry risks: a scandal can drag the brand down with them, and a star who endorses many products can seem less sincere.
segments.tr: Họ cũng mang theo rủi ro: một vụ bê bối có thể kéo thương hiệu đi xuống cùng họ, và một ngôi sao chứng thực nhiều sản phẩm có thể bị coi là thiếu chân thành.

segments.src: Influencers often have smaller audiences, but their followers may feel a **parasocial relationship**, a one-sided sense of knowing them personally.
segments.tr: Người có ảnh hưởng thường có lượng khán giả nhỏ hơn, nhưng người theo dõi họ có thể cảm thấy có **mối quan hệ xã hội giả** (parasocial), tức cảm giác một chiều rằng mình thân quen với họ.

segments.src: That feeling of closeness can make a recommendation feel like advice from a friend.
segments.tr: Cảm giác gần gũi đó có thể khiến một lời giới thiệu nghe như lời khuyên từ một người bạn.

segments.src: One more twist is the **sleeper effect**.
segments.tr: Một điểm xoắn nữa là **hiệu ứng ngủ đông (sleeper effect)**.

segments.src: Sometimes a message from a low-credibility source gains persuasive power over time, because people remember the message but forget where it came from.
segments.tr: Đôi khi, một thông điệp đến từ nguồn có độ tin cậy thấp lại tăng sức thuyết phục theo thời gian, vì người ta nhớ nội dung nhưng quên mất nguồn gốc.

segments.src: Researchers have found the effect is real but shows up only under fairly specific conditions, so don't count on it as a strategy.
segments.tr: Các nhà nghiên cứu nhận thấy hiệu ứng này có thật nhưng chỉ xuất hiện trong những điều kiện khá cụ thể, nên đừng coi nó là một chiến lược để trông cậy.

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Thuật ngữ hôm nay

segments.src: - **Source effect:** The way a message's persuasiveness changes depending on who delivers it.
segments.tr: - **Hiệu ứng nguồn:** Cách sức thuyết phục của một thông điệp thay đổi tùy theo người truyền đạt.

segments.src: - **Source credibility:** How much expertise and trustworthiness an audience sees in a messenger.
segments.tr: - **Độ tin cậy của nguồn:** Mức độ chuyên môn và tính trung thực mà khán giả thấy ở người truyền đạt.

segments.src: - **Match-up hypothesis:** The idea that an endorser is most effective when their image fits the product.
segments.tr: - **Giả thuyết ghép đôi:** Ý tưởng rằng người chứng thực hiệu quả nhất khi hình ảnh của họ phù hợp với sản phẩm.

segments.src: - **Meaning transfer:** The process by which cultural meanings tied to a celebrity carry over to an endorsed brand.
segments.tr: - **Chuyển giao ý nghĩa:** Quá trình các ý nghĩa văn hóa gắn với người nổi tiếng được chuyển sang thương hiệu được chứng thực.

segments.src: - **Parasocial relationship:** A one-sided feeling of personal connection with a media figure.
segments.tr: - **Mối quan hệ xã hội giả:** Cảm giác kết nối cá nhân một chiều với nhân vật truyền thông.

segments.src: *Answers: Q1 – B.
segments.tr: *Đáp án: Câu 1 – B.

segments.src: Credibility comes down to whether the source knows the topic (expertise) and whether they're being honest (trustworthiness).
segments.tr: Độ tin cậy phụ thuộc vào việc nguồn có hiểu chủ đề hay không (chuyên môn) và họ có trung thực hay không (tính trung thực).

segments.src: Fit matters.
segments.tr: Sự phù hợp mới là điều quan trọng.

segments.src: A famous endorser who doesn't match the product can be less effective than a less famous one who does.
segments.tr: Một người nổi tiếng chứng thực sản phẩm không phù hợp có thể kém hiệu quả hơn một người ít nổi tiếng hơn nhưng phù hợp.

segments.src: Q3 – C.
segments.tr: Câu 3 – C.

segments.src: A parasocial relationship is a one-sided sense of intimacy, and it's a big part of why influencer recommendations can feel like advice from a friend.*
segments.tr: Mối quan hệ xã hội giả là cảm giác thân mật một chiều, và đó là lý do lớn khiến lời giới thiệu từ người có ảnh hưởng có thể nghe như lời khuyên của một người bạn.*
